title_en: Certified Public Accountants Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of giving play to the role of certified public accountants in verification and service in social and economic activities, strengthening the administration of certified public accountants, safeguarding public interests and the legitimate rights and interests of investors, and promoting the healthy development of the socialist market economy.

Article 2 Certified public accountants are practicing professionals who have obtained certified public accountant certificates according to law and accept engagements to provide audit, accounting consulting, and accounting services.

Article 3 An accounting firm is an institution established according to law that undertakes the business of certified public accountants.
A certified public accountant shall join an accounting firm to practice.

Article 4 The Institute of Certified Public Accountants is a social organization composed of certified public accountants. The Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants is the national organization of certified public accountants, and the institutes of certified public accountants of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government are the local organizations of certified public accountants.

Article 5 The finance department of the State Council and the finance departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, according to law, supervise and guide certified public accountants, accounting firms, and the institutes of certified public accountants.

Article 6 Certified public accountants and accounting firms must comply with laws and administrative regulations when practicing.
Certified public accountants and accounting firms shall practice independently and impartially according to law, and are protected by law.

Article 7 The State shall implement a national unified examination system for certified public accountants. The measures for the national unified examination for certified public accountants shall be formulated by the finance department of the State Council and organized and implemented by the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Article 8 Chinese citizens who have graduated from institutions of higher learning with a college diploma or above, or who have a medium-level or above technical title in accounting or related specialties, may apply to take the national unified examination for certified public accountants; persons who have a senior technical title in accounting or related specialties may be exempted from the examination on some subjects.

Article 9 Persons who have passed the national unified examination for certified public accountants and have engaged in audit work for more than two years may apply to the institute of certified public accountants of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for registration.
Unless the circumstances listed in Article 10 of this Law exist, the institute of certified public accountants that accepts the application shall grant registration.

Article 11 The institute of certified public accountants shall report the list of persons granted registration to the finance department of the State Council for record. If the finance department of the State Council finds that the registration by the institute of certified public accountants does not conform to the provisions of this Law, it shall notify the relevant institute of certified public accountants to revoke the registration.
If the institute of certified public accountants refuses to grant registration in accordance with Article 10 of this Law, it shall notify the applicant in writing within fifteen days from the date of the decision. If the applicant has objections, he or she may, within fifteen days from receipt of the notice, apply to the finance department of the State Council or the finance department of the people's government of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for reconsideration.

Article 12 The institute of certified public accountants shall issue to an applicant who has been granted registration the certified public accountant certificate uniformly formulated by the finance department of the State Council.
Article 15 Certified public accountants may undertake accounting consulting and accounting services.

Article 16 When a certified public accountant undertakes a service, the accounting firm to which the certified public accountant belongs shall accept the engagement uniformly and enter into an engagement contract with the client.
The accounting firm shall bear civil liability for the services undertaken by the certified public accountant of the firm in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 17 When practicing, a certified public accountant may, as needed, consult the client's relevant accounting materials and documents, inspect the client's business premises and facilities, and require the client to provide other necessary assistance.
Article 18 If a certified public accountant has an interest in the client, the certified public accountant shall withdraw; the client shall have the right to request the withdrawal.
Article 19 A certified public accountant shall bear the obligation of confidentiality with respect to trade secrets known in the course of practicing.

Article 23 An accounting firm may be established as a partnership by certified public accountants.
The debts of an accounting firm established as a partnership shall be borne by the partners with their respective properties in proportion to their capital contributions or as agreed in the agreement. The partners shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of the accounting firm.

Article 26 The approving authority shall decide whether to grant approval within 30 days from the date of receiving the application documents.
An accounting firm approved by the finance department of the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be reported to the finance department of the State Council for the record. If the finance department of the State Council finds that the approval is improper, it shall, within 30 days from the date of receiving the record report, notify the original approving authority to undertake a re-examination.

Article 27 The establishment of a branch by an accounting firm must be approved by the finance department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the branch is located.

Article 28 An accounting firm shall pay taxes according to law.
An accounting firm shall establish a professional risk fund and arrange professional insurance in accordance with the provisions of the finance department of the State Council.
Article 29 An accounting firm may accept business without being restricted by administrative divisions or industries, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations.
Article 30 When a client entrusts an accounting firm to handle business, no unit or individual may interfere.
Article 31 The provisions of Articles 18 through 21 of this Law shall apply to accounting firms.
Article 32 An accounting firm shall not engage in the acts listed in subparagraphs (1) through (4), (6), and (7) of Article 22 of this Law.
Article 33 A certified public accountant shall join the Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Article 34 The articles of association of the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants shall be formulated by the National Congress of Members and reported to the finance department of the State Council for the record; the articles of association of the institute of certified public accountants of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be formulated by the congress of members of that province, autonomous region, or municipality and reported to the finance department of the people's government of that province, autonomous region, or municipality for the record.

Article 35 The Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants shall, according to law, draft the professional standards and rules for certified public accountants, and submit them to the finance department of the State Council for approval before they come into force.

Article 36 The Institute of Certified Public Accountants shall support certified public accountants in performing their business according to law, safeguard their lawful rights and interests, and reflect their opinions and suggestions to the relevant parties.
Article 37 The Institute of Certified Public Accountants shall conduct an annual inspection of the qualification and practice status of certified public accountants.
Article 38 The Institute of Certified Public Accountants shall, according to law, obtain the status of a legal person of a social organization.

Article 39 Where an accounting firm violates the provisions of Articles 20 and 21 of this Law, the finance department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall give it a warning, confiscate the illegal gains, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if the circumstances are serious, the finance department of the people's government at or above the provincial level may also suspend its business operations or revoke it.
Where a certified public accountant violates the provisions of Articles 20 and 21 of this Law, the finance department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall give a warning; if the circumstances are serious, the finance department of the people's government at or above the provincial level may suspend his/her practice or revoke his/her certified public accountant certificate.
Where an accounting firm or a certified public accountant, in violation of the provisions of Articles 20 and 21 of this Law, intentionally issues a false audit report or capital verification report, which constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 40 Where a unit undertakes the certified public accountant business as provided for in Article 14 of this Law without approval, the finance department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order it to cease the illegal activities, confiscate the illegal gains, and may concurrently impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains.

Article 41 If a party is dissatisfied with an administrative penalty decision, it may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the penalty notice, apply for reconsideration to the authority at the next higher level than the authority that made the penalty decision; the party may also, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the penalty decision notice, directly file a prosecution with the People's Court.
The reconsideration authority shall make a reconsideration decision within 60 days from the date of receipt of the reconsideration application. If a party is dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, it may file a prosecution with the People's Court within 15 days from the date of receipt of the reconsideration decision. If the reconsideration authority fails to make a reconsideration decision within the time limit, the party may file a prosecution with the People's Court within 15 days from the date of expiration of the reconsideration period.
If a party fails to apply for reconsideration within the time limit, does not file a prosecution with the People's Court, and does not comply with the penalty decision, the authority that made the penalty decision may apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.
Article 42 Where an accounting firm violates the provisions of this Law and causes losses to the client or other interested parties, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 43 A registered auditor working in an audit firm who is recognized as having the qualification of a certified public accountant may carry out the business prescribed in this Law. The measures for the recognition of their qualifications and for their supervision, guidance, and administration shall be separately prescribed by the State Council.

Article 44 The application of foreigners to take the national unified examination for Chinese certified public accountants and to register shall be handled in accordance with the principle of reciprocity.
If a foreign accounting firm needs to temporarily handle relevant business within the territory of China, it shall be subject to the approval of the financial department of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
Article 45 The State Council may, in accordance with this Law, formulate implementing regulations.

Article 46 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 1994. The Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Certified Public Accountants promulgated by the State Council on July 3, 1986 shall be abolished simultaneously.
